name: Alexander Barclay
credit: Woodcut of Barclay presenting his book to Thomas Cornish, from Pynson’s The Shyp of Folys of the Worlde, 1509 · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Alexander Barclay was a priest and poet whose birthplace is uncertain: Scotland and the English West Country have both been claimed for him. While chaplain at the College of St Mary Otery in Devon he made the English version of The Ship of Fools that Richard Pynson printed in London in 1509. He later became a Benedictine monk at Ely and afterwards a Franciscan, and died in 1552.

Barclay’s Ship of Fools is a free, much expanded translation of Sebastian Brant’s German Narrenschiff (1494), made with the help of Jacob Locher’s Latin version and a French one. It sets each kind of folly, from useless book-collecting to dishonest lawyers, before the reader in rime-royal stanzas, and adds a good deal of English satire on clergy, courtiers and the commons. He also wrote the Eclogues, among the earliest pastorals in English.
